ops.title: RolePath alias invariant: ~/.cc-review/v1/bin/cc-review must be a symlink
ops.body:
The state-dir role path `~/.cc-review/v1/bin/cc-review` is a **trust alias, never a real file**. daemonkit's protected-session classifier (`daemonrole/classifier.go`, dep v0.4.2) admits a peer to the lifecycle plane (health/shutdown/handoff) only when `peer.Executable == filepath.EvalSymlinks(RolePath)`, resolved fresh per classify. The path is the trust boundary — build strings and binary bytes are irrelevant to it.

**Wedge signature** (hit 2026-07-22 after a local binary swap `cp`'d the Caskroom binary over the alias):
- Every CLI call fails after exactly 30s: `ensure target running: child process not running: child did not come up on …daemon.sock within 30s` — while the daemon is healthy (REST answers, established channel conns live).
- `cc-review status` surfaces the true error instantly: `wire: lifecycle health outcome rejected: wire: protected session required`.
- Diagnosis: `ls -l ~/.cc-review/v1/bin/cc-review` — a regular file there is the corruption. `EvalSymlinks` of a regular file is itself, so no CLI ever matches; `Available()` stays false; `EnsureRunning` spawns a child that can't bind the held socket.

**Recovery**: `rm ~/.cc-review/v1/bin/cc-review && cc-review status` — `provision` (`internal/daemonrole/role.go`) rebuilds the symlink from the calling binary. No daemon restart needed (classify resolves the alias per call). Dev swaps must symlink the alias at a dev build, never `cp` a binary onto it.

Mechanism notes: only the lifecycle route needs protected sessions — the business route checks build strings only, so mcp-channel traffic keeps working while every `ensure`-gated CLI call is dead, which masks the break. `provision` (pre-hardening) kept any same-version regular file (`!dkversion.Newer` → keep), making the corruption permanent; hardening in progress makes a non-symlink role file re-alias at same version.

Upstream papercut (daemonkit v0.4.2): `Spawn.EnsureRunning`/launcher `Available()` swallow the health rejection reason — the surfaced error is the misleading spawn timeout, and only a non-spawning call (`status`) reveals `protected session required`.

Related: the v0.21.3 REST-nil-DB root-cause note (cc-interact `DB()` nil pre-activation).
